name: The Music of the Primes, explorable
author: Michal Takac
summary: An explorable guide to Alessandro Maria Masullo's manuscript The Music of the Primes, a proposed proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Hecke L-functions of number fields. Seven chapters build up the mathematics with live figures: prime counting, the zeta function, the explicit formula, L-functions, adeles, trace formulas, and the manuscript's strategy. The manuscript is an unrefereed draft, and the guide does not vouch for the proof.

pages.title: The music of the primes
pages.blurb: The mathematics behind a proposed proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis, with figures you can change by hand.

pages.title: Counting primes
pages.blurb: The primes look scattered. Count them and a shape appears, with a tremor on top.

pages.title: A function that knows every prime
pages.blurb: Euler's product, the complex plane, and the points where zeta vanishes.

pages.title: Zeros as notes
pages.blurb: Each zero is a wave. Add them up and the primes come out. The Riemann hypothesis fixes the volume.

pages.title: The whole family of L-functions
pages.blurb: Characters sort primes into classes. The generalized hypothesis covers all of them.

pages.title: Every prime's point of view
pages.blurb: Sizes measured prime by prime, shells inside p-adic balls, and functions folded over the rationals.

pages.title: Two ways to count the same thing
pages.blurb: A loop, a smear, and a number computed twice. Each prime is a loop of length log p.

pages.title: The strategy of the manuscript
pages.blurb: One prime at a time, in a room where only nearby zeros can be heard.

pages.title: Status, sources, glossary
pages.blurb: What the manuscript contains today, what is unfinished, and where to read more.
